title: MelissaDL x Breed: Towards Data-Efficient On-line Supervised Training of Multi-parametric Surrogates with Active Learning
problem: Traditional offline training of neural network surrogates for PDEs requires pre-computing entire datasets with numerical solvers, causing prohibitive storage and I/O costs. Online training requires strategies to efficiently select which simulation samples to generate and use for training.
motivation: Neural network surrogates can dramatically accelerate scientific simulations, but data acquisition and training efficiency are critical bottlenecks limiting practical adoption in HPC workflows.
method: The approach generates training data on-the-fly during learning instead of pre-computing everything, with Melissa handling the streaming pipeline and Breed selecting which simulations to generate. Breed analyzes training loss statistics to find where the model performs poorly, then focuses new simulations on those difficult regions of the parameter space. It uses Adaptive Multiple Importance Sampling (AMIS: a technique that reweights simulation candidates as the model learns). The neural network learns to predict specified timesteps into the future for any combination of initial and boundary conditions.
key_novelty: Combining training loss statistics with Adaptive Multiple Importance Sampling (a technique that reweights simulation candidates based on learning progress) to intelligently select which simulations to generate, focusing computational effort on parameter space regions where the model performs poorly.
contributions: Breed active learning method using AMIS guided by training loss statistics for online surrogate training
Multi-parametric direct surrogate architecture trained with streaming data
Demonstration of improved generalization with reduced computational overhead compared to offline approaches
Validation on 2D heat PDE showing data-efficiency gains from selective sampling

metrics.other: reduced computational overhead versus baseline approaches

limitations: Preliminary results limited to 2D heat PDE; generalization to higher dimensions and more complex PDEs not evaluated.
primary_theme: data-efficient neural surrogates via importance-sampled active learning
